stem: Contrary to what might be expected, having numerous relationships is not necessarily a ____ loneliness since loneliness is determined by the way people experience relationships subjectively.

During Roosevelt's first meeting with President Harrison, Harrison seemed less ____ than usual: having just returned from a salubrious cruise down the Potomac, his characteristic sour silence was replaced by a ruddy, clear-eyed demeanor.

Whereas in the early nineteenth century phrenologists had seen every part of the brain surface as the seat of a specific intellectual or moral faculty, the 1830s and 1840s saw a (i)____ of this belief, to such an extent that the brain came to be seen as (ii)____.
colsZh: 得到辩护；证明无罪；正确

stem: One of the problems with recent books that perpetuate the view of Jane Austen as moral tutor, a sort of Miss Manners for the ages, is that they understand manners as (i)____, as near-universal and timeless behavioral ideals or, worse still, a set of rules to be followed. It is crucial, however, to (ii)____. In other words, one needs to resist (iii)____ generic “manners” with more linguistically and historically precise designations, no least because Austen herself distinguishes.
colsZh: 将不同的行为混为一谈

stem: A telescope orbiting in space, above the unruly atmosphere, is able to detect ultraviolet and infrared emissions that are blocked by Earth’s atmosphere and thus ____ to astronomers on the ground.
Walking appears simple, yet every step forward is a ____ act: each step is essentially a fall that one must catch by swinging one’s leg forward so that one’s foot lands on the floor just in time.

Scholars of the civil rights movement have often characterized it as springing from social, political, and economic structures ____ the South, thus overlooking the tradition of civil rights activism in other regions of the country.
